# Copilot instructions

Follow [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). It is the canonical rule set for this repository, and it takes precedence over anything in this file. This file adds only Copilot-specific guidance.

- Path-specific rules in `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` apply automatically to matching files: storage, and the HTTP API and CLI.
- Copilot Chat in VS Code: the workspace's `.vscode/mcp.json` names the MCP servers.
  - `polaroid-agent` (the endpoint configured in `.vscode/mcp.json`) is the procedural knowledge interface. Begin each task in this workspace by calling `discover` with repository `github.com/ashuangiras/polaroid` and a task string containing `polaroid.using`, then `read` that exact candidate at the returned snapshot, even when lexical ranking places another candidate above it. For discovery context, use the task in your own words and the canonical repository identifier when known. With v7, start the root using `allow_dynamic_children: true` at that snapshot. For this repository, discover/read `polaroid.session-close-capture` at the same snapshot and attach it immediately; leave it pending until task-specific work and verification are complete. Discover/read relevant task procedures at that snapshot and attach them dynamically as work is selected; advance their leaves, then perform the capture child last. Capture only reusable, evidence-backed knowledge; a no-op is correct when no supported learning exists. The capture child may publish locally through complete field-review proposals after validation succeeds; this is the single standing authorization in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), not permission for other automatic proposals or remote pushes. Do not close or report the root complete until the capture child and all task children are done and the parent status is `complete`. Additional task children may still be attached while the parent token is open, reopening it after a prior `complete`. On v1-v6, `start`/`advance` cannot track runtime-discovered children; report that limitation rather than claiming this workflow gate. Use `resolve` when typed-record reasoning matters. Discovery is lexical, so judge relevance rather than assuming every match applies. `feedback` is for genuine problems with existing procedures, not new session knowledge. The MCP parent is a cross-host workflow gate, not a host-enforced block: clients may ignore or abandon it. [docs/architecture/knowledge-guide.md](../docs/architecture/knowledge-guide.md) is the full usage guide. This is the only Polaroid server configured here: the legacy `/mcp` (42 tools) is deliberately not wired into this workspace, so it cannot be reached by accident. Operator and evidence work it would have served — binding resolution, execution recording, feedback triage — is done with the `polaroid` CLI instead.
  - `dispatch` runs commands and keeps their output.

  `polaroid-agent` and `dispatch` are local entries. If a server's tools are missing or stale after the service is upgraded, restart that MCP server and open a new chat: a chat keeps the tool list it started with.
- Copilot cloud agent: the Go toolchain comes from `go.mod` (the `toolchain` line), and golangci-lint must be 2.14.0. Before you push, run the gate of the binding that matches your change (AGENTS.md, "Before you call it done"). The `ci` workflow runs only when dispatched by hand; do not wait for it. If a tool is missing in your environment, report that check as not run. Never report it as passed.
- Copilot code review: flag any change that does one of these things:
  - rewrites stored history, or edits an applied migration;
  - adds task-specific behavior to code;
  - imports HTTP or storage packages into `internal/memory`;
  - returns internal error text to clients;
  - changes the API or record contract without updating `docs/architecture/`;
  - adds behavior without tests;
  - reports a scoped verification (`verify-docs`, `verify-records`, `verify-focused`) as verification of the commit, or uses one for a change it excludes.
